# Test fixtures

Shared, **synthetic** sample data. Never commit real customer data: names, e-mails and phone
numbers in these files are invented (`example.com`, `+39 000 000000x`).

`.gitattributes` marks `tests/fixtures/**` as `-text`: bytes are stored exactly as written, so the
UTF-8 BOM and Windows-1252 files keep their encoding on every platform.

## `bookings/` (Gate 2)

| File | Purpose |
| ---- | ------- |
| `en_comma.csv` | English headers, comma, ISO dates |
| `it_semicolon.csv` | Italian headers, semicolon, day-first dates, decimal comma and thousands dot |
| `utf8_bom.csv` | the English file with a UTF-8 BOM |
| `cp1252.csv` | Italian file in Windows-1252 with accented text |
| `pii_unmapped_columns.csv` | guest name / e-mail / phone / notes columns that must never be persisted |
| `unknown_status.csv` | a status value that is not recognised (row must be reported, not defaulted) |
| `ambiguous_dates.csv` | day/month-first dates that need a configured format |
| `duplicate_source_id.csv` | the same source record id twice in one file |
| `invalid_row.csv` | a row with a negative amount, zero rooms and check-out before check-in |
| `changed_schema.csv` | a mapped column (`Check-in`) renamed |
| `masseria_ninfa_bookings_v1.csv` | **golden mini import**: 16 bookings of a fictional agriturismo (direct, Booking.com-like labels, Expedia, Airbnb, an agency, a tour operator; confirmed, cancelled, no-show; lead times from days to months; commissions, room types, a booking made right after the spring clock change) |
| `masseria_ninfa_bookings_v1.expected.json` | its canonical result, computed **independently of the application code** with the standard library only (`csv`, `zoneinfo`, `decimal`); rows MN-0001, MN-0009 (booked at 03:30 on the spring clock-change day: the skipped hour is deliberately not used, a naive local time in it is rejected) and MN-0016 were also checked by hand |

XLSX files are generated by the tests (`tests/booking_support.py`) instead of being committed as
binaries. The golden result is only source file → canonical bookings: no metric or decision is
derived from it.

## `snapshots/` (Gate 3)

| File | Purpose |
| ---- | ------- |
| `masseria_ninfa_bookings_addendum_v1.csv` | 7 synthetic bookings added to the Gate 2 golden world (same Italian headers, imported through the same mapping): a checked-in multi-room booking, a checked-out one, a no-show, a cancellation **without** a cancellation date (2 rooms), a booking on a closed night, and revenue that no whole number of cents divides evenly over the nights (`100,00` over 3 nights, `1.000,00` over 3, `200,01` over 2) |
| `masseria_ninfa_snapshots_v1.expected.json` | the declared **room inventory** (with a closed period and a period with no row), the instants of the observed and reconstructed runs, 39 hand-checkable probes (each with the reason it matters) and a SHA-256 of the whole grid of 207 snapshot days × 124 stay nights |
| `generate_masseria_snapshots_expected.py` | computes that expected file from the two CSVs with the **standard library only** (`csv`, `decimal`, `zoneinfo`, `datetime`, `hashlib`, `json`), sharing no code with the application; run it with any Python 3.11+ |

It is BOOKINGS + INVENTORY -> SNAPSHOTS only: no expected value, alert, impact, priority,
recommendation or decision is derived from it. Guest names and phone numbers in the CSVs are
invented (`+39 000 0000101`...) and must never reach a snapshot (a test checks it).

## `expected/` (Gate 4)

| File | Purpose |
| ---- | ------- |
| `masseria_ninfa_bookings_history_v1.csv` | 252 synthetic history bookings (fictional guests `Ospite Storico 0001...`, phones `+39 000 9000001...`, one-night stays) that extend the Gate 2/3 golden world so that the Expected Engine has comparables |
| `masseria_ninfa_expected_v1.expected.json` | the snapshots to materialise (154: 42 OBSERVED since the fictional "observation start" 2026-04-01, 112 RECONSTRUCTED), a checksum of their independently computed values, and the 6 expected baselines with every comparable used |
| `generate_masseria_expected_expected.py` | writes both files with the **standard library only** (`csv`, `fractions`, `datetime`, `hashlib`, `json`), sharing no code with the application (exact fractions instead of `Decimal`, its own calendar and statistics); it reuses only the Gate 3 generator's brute-force snapshot cell, which is independent too |

Six targets, each on its own weekday so that no stay date is shared: **A** Sat 2026-08-15 at 14 days
(observed only, low dispersion, plus distractors of every kind: wrong lead time 13 and 15, same weekday
out of season, same season wrong weekday, a stay after the target seen after its snapshot day, a stay
older than 730 days); **B** Sun 2026-08-16 at 7 days (observed only, high dispersion, `LOW`
confidence); **C** Sat 2026-05-09 at 14 days (3 observed + 19 clean reconstructions; 2 uncertain
reconstructions rejected; capped at 85); **D** Tue 2026-07-07 at 21 days (only 4 comparables exist:
`INSUFFICIENT_DATA`); **E** Fri 2026-04-24 at 10 days (24 comparables, **12 of them with zero rooms**; fractional
median 0.50); **F** Thu 2026-05-21 at 50 days (reconstructed only: capped at 65).

Checked by hand (independently of both the application and the generator's code paths): **A** sample
`11, 11, 12, 13, 13, 13` -> median (12+13)/2 = 12.50; P25 at position 1.25 = 11 + 0.25*(12-11) = 11.25;
P75 at position 3.75 = 13; IQR 1.75; confidence 0.40*50 + 0.35*100 + 0.25*(100 - 50*1.75/12.5 = 93)
= 20 + 35 + 23.25 = **78.25** (MEDIUM). **B** sample `0, 1, 2, 24, 26, 31` -> median (2+24)/2 = 13.00;
P25 = 1 + 0.25*(2-1) = 1.25; P75 = 24 + 0.75*(26-24) = 25.50; IQR 24.25; stability 100 - 50*24.25/13 = 6.73;
confidence 20 + 35 + 1.68 = **56.68** (LOW). **F** 24 reconstructed comparables, median 7.00, IQR 2:
formula 40 + 21 + 0.25*85.71 = 82.43 -> capped by the 85 rule and then by the 65 rule = **65.00**.
**D** has 4 comparables: no number at all.

It is BOOKINGS -> SNAPSHOTS -> EXPECTED BASELINES only: no alert, impact, priority, recommendation or
decision is derived from it. Guest names and phone numbers are invented and must never reach a
snapshot or a baseline (a test checks it).
